In [[geometry]], the '''elongated pentagonal orthobirotunda''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|42}}}}). Its [[Conway polyhedron notation]] is [https://levskaya.github.io/polyhedronisme/?recipe=at5jP5&palette=%230000ff%20%23ffee00%20%2300ff00%20%23ff0000 at5jP5]. As the name suggests, it can be constructed by elongating a [[pentagonal orthobirotunda]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|34}}}}) by inserting a [[decagonal prism]] between its congruent halves. Rotating one of the [[pentagonal rotunda]]e ({{math|''J''{{sub|6}}}}) through 36&nbsp;degrees before inserting the prism yields the [[elongated pentagonal gyrobirotunda]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|43}}}}).

{{Johnson solid}}
[[File:J42 elongated pentagonal orthobirotunda.stl|thumb|3D model of an elongated pentagonal orthobirotunda]]

==Formulae==
The following [[formula]]e for [[volume]] and [[surface area]] can be used if all [[faces (geometry)|faces]] are [[regular polygon|regular]], with edge length ''a'':<ref>[[Stephen Wolfram]], "[http://www.wolframalpha.com/input/?i=Elongated+pentagonal+orthobirotunda Elongated pentagonal orthobirotunda]" from [[Wolfram Alpha]]. Retrieved July 26, 2010.</ref>

:<math>V=\frac{1}{6}\left(45+17\sqrt{5}+15\sqrt{5+2\sqrt{5}}\right)a^3\approx21.5297...a^3</math>

:<math>A=\left(10+\sqrt{30\left(10+3\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{75+30\sqrt{5}}\right)}\right)a^2\approx39.306...a^2</math>
